Paralympic Games = the major international multi-sport event for athletes with disabilities
Grand Slam = one of the four major tennis tournaments, or winning all four in a year
world record = the best official result ever achieved in an event
knockout stage = the part of a tournament in which losing means elimination
group stage = the opening round in which teams play in small groups
opening ceremony = the official show that starts a major championship or Games
medal ceremony = the official presentation of medals after an event
seeded player = a highly ranked competitor given a favourable place in the draw
heat = an early race that decides who reaches the next round
kick-off = the first kick that starts a football match; the scheduled start time
referee = the official who controls a football, rugby or boxing contest
umpire = the official who controls tennis, cricket, volleyball or badminton
assistant referee = an official who helps the referee, especially with offside and throw-ins
substitute = a player who comes on in place of a teammate
spectator = a person who watches a sports event in person
hooligan = a person who causes violence or damage in connection with sport
coach = a person who trains a team or athlete
manager = the person in charge of a football club's team affairs
captain = the player who leads the team on the field
goalkeeper = the player whose job is to stop the ball going into the goal
